results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 70 body paragraphs' outline summaries match the controlling idea of the spec paragraph they align to, in spec order (p01-p69, with p22-p30/p39 lifecycle before p18-p21 invariants as the spec's section order declares); the five callouts have no spec paragraph.

Availability ¶2, flagged two_ideas by the outliner, opens with one controlling sentence ('Two rules keep this manageable.') that both rules serve, exactly as spec p38 declares; not a failure. The only other flagged unit fails below.

results.draft_locus: Vertical Differences ¶2
results.quote: Motorvane's Essen Volkswagen Golf shows the automotive ghost source: it sold on 29 April 2027, but the dealer feed's removal arrived 26 hours later
results.finding: The paragraph opens on configuration ('At Veldmark the table translates into configuration, not forks') and then turns to a late-feed ghost that configuration cannot address, with no sentence tying the two; the outliner needed two summaries. A framing that presents the Golf as the one row of the table that configuration cannot fix, only measure, would make it one idea as p54 intends.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: intro and scene to the thesis and L6; what-is to L1; identity to L2; lifecycle, availability, in-practice, verticals to L4; invariants to L3; versions to L5; architecture and bike to L5/L6; trade-offs, failure modes, CA view and questions to the claims their spec sections name.

Every table, figure, quotation and source is accompanied by a sentence saying what it shows (e.g. 'The table does: each neighbor has its own identity and lifetime...', 'Both are external-key designs...', 'The pattern is consistent...', 'A dealer listing that shows "price reduced" must therefore be backed by a price series...', 'The replay shows the aggregate changing only for facts about the offer...', 'Veldmark's March 2027 audit found the problem was not rare'); figures 1-5 carry explanatory captions.

All other boundaries express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information, e.g. 'Identity names the listing; the lifecycle gives its state.', 'With the states defined, which rules must always hold?', 'The sold transition so far assumes one thing that sells once', 'Every transition, edit and change of quantity leaves a trace.', 'Public contracts show a lifecycle's edges; a replay shows its inside.', 'Group-scale decisions prevent these failures.', 'So what was the state of Femke's bike at 08:00 on Tuesday?'.

results.draft_locus: The Lifecycle: Two Dimensions, Not One Status ¶9
results.quote: **Expiry is a data-quality control, not just a revenue lever.**
results.finding: Spec p29 declares a contrast with renewal as a ranking act (carries over 'Renewal as a ranking act'). The opening contrasts expiry with a revenue lever instead, and the previous paragraph's renewal/bump point is not picked up until the paragraph's last sentences, so the boundary does not express the declared relationship.

results.quote: Some attributes change meaning without anyone editing the listing.
results.finding: Spec p36 declares similarity with price as a time series. The opening sentence does not pick up the price series or signal that these facts are kept the same way; the likeness (an effective date and a source) appears only at the paragraph's end.

results.draft_locus: Availability, Units and Multi-Item Listings ¶1
results.quote: The sold transition so far assumes one thing that sells once, and not every listing offers that.
results.finding: Both flow readers could explain the Availability section's position only weakly: it qualifies the sold transition, so it belongs next to the lifecycle, yet it sits after the invariants and breaks the invariants-to-versions link (material edits). Both proposed the same reorder (lifecycle, availability, invariants, versions). The spec's flow rationale justifies 'availability follows' only by the sold transition, which argues for placing it after the lifecycle, so the difficulty comes from the declared order itself.

results.finding: The introduction opens with an intriguing example (the fifteen-year-old `ads` table), bridges to Part II's claim, states the test and gives a roadmap; none of the five weak patterns.

The conclusion opens by answering the scene's question, synthesizes, gives the so-what and hands off to categories as the spec's declared hand-off; no 'in conclusion', no new subtopic, no body evidence.

'Each system that went wrong exposed a different missing rule ... Only the rules together answer the chapter's test for every copy, and they are the agreement Sven's contract needed. Ghost inventory then becomes a measure per consumer, fixed in the copy that missed the event rather than in search.' states what no single section states and why it matters.

Returns to Ingrid's question ('So what was the state of Femke's bike at 08:00 on Tuesday?') with one answer (sold, no enforcement, version 9, outcome sold on platform, €225) and why each system was wrong.

The reader predicted all fifteen sections in the draft's (and spec's) section order, the evidence (fictional Veldmark and the bike; public APIs and standards) and the tone. Note: AC-2's expected text lists invariants before the lifecycle, the reverse of the spec's own section order; the reader's prediction matches the spec's sections.

The reader locates the failure in the digest copy, not search (assembled at 17:30 from a pre-sale snapshot, nothing re-checked), and names the fixes in the chapter's terms: versioned events for sold/expired/withdrawn/blocked, a declared removal deadline per consumer, re-check at send / purge on removal. The reader did not mention the sale price as an outcome; the probe gives no sale price and does not ask about analytics, so that element of expected is not elicited by the probe; the chapter states it (replay ¶2).

Matches expected: three owners on one status field so one overwrites another (resume set status = active); publication state owned by the listing (seller and clock) plus an enforcement overlay owned by trust and safety, visibility derived from both; no seller command may lift a block, enforced by the listing service as an invariant on every seller command.

Matches expected on all four: (a) invariant, listing service against the category schema at submission and on edits of an active listing, not in draft; (b) policy, asynchronous duplicate detection after publish; (c) policy, entitlement service at publish with a reservation, reconciled later; (d) invariant, listing service on every command, a bump moves only ranked_at.
